cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: For the Record
cards.instruction: Get someone to state exactly what they did, knew, or authorized before you reveal your own involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Before I show you my dinner invitations, who did you authorize your sister to bring?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A date. Did you invite my ex?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Did you name anyone she couldn't bring? Then we'll get to my list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. My ex. I sent you both the same message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What time did you send it to me? I'll put that beside my invitation's timestamp before we open it.

mechanism: Copy invitation annotations as confident organizing, then seek the exact guest permissions before exposing what was sent.
confusable: Not merely an invitation mistake: B2 identifies misunderstood plus-one marks, A3 masks confusion and demands the permission record.
comparison: Intimate wedding guest dispute uses a copied annotation rather than workplace terminology.
seedUse: Retains the canonical Drive withheld invitations and Tuesday-message timing tactic; changes dinner to wedding to make plus-one imitation concrete.
